Experiment 2 uses 0.10 mol of Mg ribbon with excess HCl at the same temperature and concentration.
Comparing the volume of H2 gas produced over time:
correct_answer: Experiment 2 produces twice the final volume of H2 gas compared to Experiment 1 because the limiting reactant (Mg) is doubled.
wrong_answers_pool: Both experiments produce the exact same final volume because HCl is in excess.
Experiment 1 produces more gas because ribbon has greater surface area.
Experiment 2 produces less gas due to rapid depletion of acid.
Experiment 2 takes four times as long to finish.
Experiment 1 has a steeper initial gradient than Experiment 2.
The volume of gas is independent of the moles of magnesium.

question: [Exam Question 64] A science class analyzes reaction curves: In an experiment, 2 g of pure calcium carbonate granules reacts with excess 1 mol·dm⁻³ HCl at 25 °C (Curve A). In a second experiment, 2 g of calcium carbonate powder is used with the same acid at 25 °C (Curve B). What will be observed on the graph of volume of CO2 gas vs time?
correct_answer: Curve B has a steeper initial gradient (faster rate) but reaches the exact same final volume of CO2 as Curve A at a shorter time (because the limiting reagent quantity is unchanged).
wrong_answers_pool: Curve B produces double the volume of CO2 because powder has more surface area.
Curve B has a gentler slope because powder dissolves more slowly.
Curve A produces a greater total volume of CO2 because granules last longer.
Curve B reaches a lower final volume because powder reacts too violently.
Both curves will be identical in gradient and final volume.
Curve B reaches completion at a later time than Curve A.

The two curves are exactly superimposed throughout the experiment.

Experiment 2: 0.1 mol Zn reacts with excess 1 mol·dm⁻³ HCl (Curve 2).
What is the relationship between Curve 1 and Curve 2 on a volume of H2 gas vs time graph?
correct_answer: Curve 1 has a steeper initial slope (faster rate due to higher concentration) but both curves level off at the exact same horizontal plateau (same final volume of H2 because Zn is the limiting reagent in both trials).
wrong_answers_pool: Curve 1 produces double the total volume of H2 gas because the acid concentration is double.
Curve 2 has a steeper slope because dilute acid reacts more efficiently.
Curve 2 produces twice as much gas because there is more water present.
Curve 1 finishes later than Curve 2 because the reaction is too concentrated.
Curve 1 levels off at half the volume of Curve 2.
The two curves are exactly superimposed throughout the experiment.

question:
[Exam Question 99] A science class analyzes reaction curves: Experiment 1 uses 0.05 mol of Mg ribbon with excess HCl.
Experiment 2 uses 0.10 mol of Mg ribbon with excess HCl at the same temperature and concentration.
Comparing the volume of H2 gas produced over time:
correct_answer: Experiment 2 produces twice the final volume of H2 gas compared to Experiment 1 because the limiting reactant (Mg) is doubled.
wrong_answers_pool: Both experiments produce the exact same final volume because HCl is in excess.
Experiment 1 produces more gas because ribbon has greater surface area.
Experiment 2 produces less gas due to rapid depletion of acid.
Experiment 2 takes four times as long to finish.
Experiment 1 has a steeper initial gradient than Experiment 2.
The volume of gas is independent of the moles of magnesium.
